policy: Every recovered inventory entry and every byte in Updater's initialized .text virtual range is assigned exactly once. product_application identifies Peer Pressure product behavior and reconstruction priority, not personal authorship, originality, or copyright ownership. Standalone MSVC standard-library template instantiations emitted into application translation units remain platform_toolchain rather than product logic. Inlined support instructions inherit the ownership of their containing recovered function because the inventory has no smaller defensible ownership unit. unknown is reserved for an entry whose provenance cannot be supported; this evidence set leaves that bucket empty.
scope_note: This is an ownership and prioritization artifact, not a source lift. The vendored miniz tree is pinned and attributed instead of being rewritten. Two terminal inventory entries describe linker/import metadata rather than callable functions; they are retained because the authoritative function inventory exposes them and their bytes still require exactly-once accounting.

product_application.description: Updater-specific archive wrapping, SoftmodData/XBPP parsing and selection, HDD bootstrap policy, phase-two staging, file/path policy, diagnostics, lifecycle hook, and update orchestration. The label is product provenance, not a claim about the identity of a human author.

upstream_miniz.description: The contiguous miniz decompressor and ZIP-reader implementation. It is attributed and pinned to the declared upstream release; it is outside the closed product-source reconstruction queue.

platform_toolchain.description: MSVC C++ support and emitted STL templates, Xbox/MSVC file support, process startup, CRT/unwind/math/compiler helpers, import thunks, and terminal linker metadata. Platform classification describes the supplied implementation role; it does not imply those proprietary library sources are vendored or open source.

unknown.description: No recovered entry remains unassigned after separating product routines, standalone emitted templates/support, miniz, runtime, imports, and terminal metadata.

uncertainties: Product classification is component-level provenance, not a claim that Grimdoomer or any named person personally authored every instruction in those functions.
Semantic names not already present in Updater-symbols.json are descriptive recovery labels and are not asserted to be original PDB spellings.
The exact miniz revision rests on the public author declaration plus the pinned gitlink; the binary independently proves the 3.x family but compiler optimization prevents source-text byte identity.

Standalone template bodies are separated from product logic, but compiler-inlined standard-library sequences inside a product function cannot be assigned independently without inventing sub-function ownership boundaries.

The final 48 .text bytes are linker/import metadata, including a pointer to RunUpdate, rather than executable product logic; the function-recovery inventory nevertheless exposes two entries there, so this partition accounts for them as platform/toolchain-generated metadata.
